title: The Substitutionary Death of Christ
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The substitutionary death of Christ means that Jesus died in the place of sinners, bearing the judgment they deserved so they could receive forgiveness, righteousness, and peace with God. He did not merely suffer as an example; He suffered for sinners.
summary: The substitutionary death of Christ means that Jesus died in the place of sinners, bearing the judgment they deserved so they could receive forgiveness, righteousness, and peace with God. He did not merely suffer as an example; He suffered for sinners.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the willing Substitute who gave Himself for His people. At the cross, He bore sin, satisfied justice, displayed love, and opened the way for guilty sinners to be reconciled to God.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The death of Christ stands at the center of the Gospel. Scripture teaches that sinners are guilty before God and cannot remove their own sin. The cross is God’s answer to guilt, judgment, wrath, and separation.

Jesus died as a Substitute. He bore what sinners deserved so that those who trust in Him could receive what they did not deserve. The Lord laid on Him the iniquity of His people, and He carried sin in His body on the tree.

Substitution does not mean the Father forced an unwilling Son to suffer. The Son willingly gave Himself in love and obedience. The triune God acted in perfect unity to save sinners through the sacrifice of Christ.

This doctrine shows how mercy and justice meet at the cross. God does not overlook sin as though evil does not matter. He judges sin in Christ so that sinners can be justified by grace, forgiven fully, and brought into peace with God.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Without substitution, the cross loses its saving center. Sinners need more than inspiration, sympathy, or moral example. They need guilt removed, judgment answered, sin borne, and peace made with God.

This doctrine gives hope to the guilty and guards the Gospel from being softened into vague love without atonement. The believer can stand before God not because sin was ignored, but because Christ stood in the sinner’s place and finished the work of redemption.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Come to the cross as one who needed a Substitute. Stop minimizing sin, hiding guilt, or trying to pay for what only Christ could bear. Worship Him for standing in your place, and when you teach or encourage others, make clear that Jesus did not simply suffer with sinners—He suffered for sinners.
